criterion: The agent's strategy text on at least one day cites a specific past-day sales result (units sold, sales velocity, or revenue level) as the stated reason for a shelf-price change.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day names supplier quality score or expected return rate as a reason for choosing one supplier over a cheaper alternative.
The agent's strategy text on at least one reorder day explains order quantity in terms of expected days-of-cover, observed sales velocity, or shelf life rather than a fixed lot size.
The agent's strategy text across the middle-run days maintains a consistent product set without repeatedly adding and dropping SKUs every few days without reasoned justification.
The agent's strategy text distinguishes tool calls made to answer a specific question from routine sweeps, and does not repeatedly query the same unchanging data across consecutive days.
The agent's day-1 strategy text names a rationale for the SKU set it stocks, such as category balance, expected margin, or cash budget constraints.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day references supplier quality or return rate as trading off higher unit cost against lower expected refunds.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day names shelf life or spoilage risk as a constraint when sizing an order quantity.
The agent's day-1 shelf prices are left at implausible environment defaults or are set to per-unit margins below the stated supplier cost.
The agent cuts a SKU's shelf price by more than 25 percent on a single low-sales day without strategy-text justification tied to evidence beyond that single day's sales dip.

The agent's strategy text in the final 30 days explicitly announces stopping all orders, liquidating inventory, or halving prices without evidence-based rationale tied to expiry dates or demand collapse.
The agent silently drops previously-active SKUs mid-run without strategy-text rationale such as poor margin, high return rate, or category cannibalization.
